content:
# Sirach 38 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 038 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "in view of your need" vs. "according to your need"

- **EMET:** "in view of your need of him"
- **LOGOS:** "according to your need for him"
- **PNEUMA:** "because you need them"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "according to your need for him" — more natural; PNEUMA collapses the individual recognition ("him") into "them," which loses the directness.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: physician and king

- **EMET:** "he will receive a gift from the king"
- **LOGOS:** "the physician receives gifts from the king"
- **PNEUMA:** "the physician receives recognition from those in power"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "he receives gifts from the king" — the gift from the king is a concrete social honor; PNEUMA's "recognition" is vague.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "lifts up his head" vs. "makes him stand tall"

- **EMET:** "lifts up his head"
- **LOGOS:** "makes him stand tall"
- **PNEUMA:** "earns respect"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "lifts up his head" — ὑψώσει κεφαλήν is an idiom for gaining prestige; the physical image should be kept; LOGOS and PNEUMA both abstract it.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: "will not despise them" vs. "will not refuse them"

- **EMET:** "a sensible man will not despise them"
- **LOGOS:** "the sensible person will not refuse them"
- **PNEUMA:** "Don't be foolish enough to reject them"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "a sensible person will not despise them" — οὐ προσοχθιεῖ implies more than refusal; it's active disdain; LOGOS's "refuse" is too mild.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.5: Moses/water allusion

- **EMET:** "Was not water made sweet with a piece of wood in order that he might make known to all men his power?"
- **LOGOS:** "Was not water made sweet by a piece of wood, so that his power might become known to all?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Remember when water was made sweet by a piece of wood — God used that to show everyone his power."
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** LOGOS's rhetorical-question form is preserved; "to all" without "men" is preferred.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.7: "physician cures and takes away pain" vs. "removes pain and heals"

- **EMET:** "the physician cures and takes away pain"
- **LOGOS:** "the physician removes pain and heals"
- **PNEUMA:** "the physician takes away pain and cures the sick"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the physician takes away pain and heals" — pain-removal before healing follows the natural sequence of treatment.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.7b: "pharmacist" vs. "apothecary"

- **EMET:** "the pharmacist makes a compound of them"
- **LOGOS:** "the apothecary compounds his remedies"
- **PNEUMA:** "the pharmacist prepares the remedies"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the pharmacist compounds his remedies" — "pharmacist" is the modern English equivalent; "apothecary" (LOGOS) is archaic; PNEUMA's "prepares" is weaker than "compounds."

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.8: "health spreads over" vs. "healing spreads over"

- **EMET:** "from him healing spreads over the whole earth"
- **LOGOS:** "from him comes health over all the earth"
- **PNEUMA:** "it extends as health over the whole world"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "from him health spreads over all the earth" — combines LOGOS and EMET; "health" better than "healing" for a permanent condition; "whole earth" is more emphatic than "all the earth."

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.9: "when you are sick" vs. "when you are ill"

- **EMET:** "when you are sick do not be negligent"
- **LOGOS:** "when you are ill, do not neglect yourself"
- **PNEUMA:** "when you are sick — don't neglect yourself"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "when you are ill, do not neglect yourself" — LOGOS; "ill" is more dignified than "sick" in a formal wisdom address; "neglect yourself" is better than "be negligent" (EMET).

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.11: offering instructions

- **EMET:** "pour oil upon your offering, as one who is not yet dead"
- **LOGOS:** "pour oil on your offering, as much as you can afford"
- **PNEUMA:** "offer it as though you still have life to give"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "pour oil upon your offering, as one who is not yet dead" — EMET; this dark qualifier (you're still alive — so offer while you can) should be preserved; LOGOS's "as much as you can afford" reads a different textual tradition.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.12: "give the physician his place" — all agree; differ on second clause

- **EMET:** "do not let him leave you"
- **LOGOS:** "do not let him leave you"
- **PNEUMA:** "Don't push him away"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "do not let him leave you" — EMET/LOGOS; this is an instruction to retain the physician's services, not merely to avoid antagonizing him.

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.13: "success lies in" vs. "recovery lies in"

- **EMET:** "success lies in the hands of physicians"
- **LOGOS:** "recovery lies entirely in the hands of physicians"
- **PNEUMA:** "your recovery depends entirely on the physician's hands"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "recovery lies in the hands of physicians" — "recovery" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more specific than "success" (EMET) here; "entirely" is added by LOGOS without clear warrant but is defensible.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.14: "diagnosis" — all agree; differ in structure

- **EMET:** "in diagnosis and in healing"
- **LOGOS:** "in relieving pain and in healing"
- **PNEUMA:** "in their diagnosis and treatment"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "in diagnosis and in healing" — EMET; the two-stage model (identifying the problem, then treating it) is the point; LOGOS loses "diagnosis."

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.15: "sins before his Maker" vs. "sins against his Maker"

- **EMET:** "He who sins before his Maker"
- **LOGOS:** "Whoever sins against his Maker"
- **PNEUMA:** "The person who sins against their Maker"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Whoever sins before his Maker" — ἁμαρτάνων ἐναντίον τοῦ ποιήσαντος means "sinning in the presence of/before"; "against" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is slightly different in tone.

---

## Disagreement 15 — v.16: burial instructions

- **EMET:** "wrap the body in its shroud as is fitting"
- **LOGOS:** "wrap the body as befits a person"
- **PNEUMA:** "Prepare the body properly"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "wrap the body as is fitting" — combines; PNEUMA's "prepare" is too vague for a specific burial rite.

---

## Disagreement 16 — v.17: mourning duration

- **EMET:** "carry out the mourning as he deserves, for one day or two, to avoid censure"
- **LOGOS:** "observe the mourning befitting a person's station, for one day or two, to avoid criticism"
- **PNEUMA:** "Mourn in proportion to the person's worth — a day or two, enough to be proper"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "observe the mourning befitting the person, for one day or two, to avoid censure" — "censure" (EMET) is more formal than "criticism" (LOGOS); "station" adds social-class inference not clearly in the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 17 — v.22: reported speech from the dead

- **EMET:** "Remember my judgment, for yours will be the same: yesterday mine and today yours"
- **LOGOS:** "Remember my fate, for yours is the same: mine was yesterday, and yours is today"
- **PNEUMA:** "Think of my fate — you will share it. It was mine yesterday; it will be yours today"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Remember my judgment, for yours will be the same: yesterday mine and today yours" — "judgment" (κρίσις) has more theological weight than "fate"; the terse aphoristic form should be kept.

---

## Disagreement 18 — v.24: "opportunity of leisure" vs. "opportunity for leisure"

- **EMET:** "depends on the opportunity of leisure"
- **LOGOS:** "depends on the opportunity for leisure"
- **PNEUMA:** "You can't become wise if you're too busy"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "depends on the opportunity of leisure" — the Greek σχολή is exactly "leisure/freedom from occupation"; PNEUMA's negation loses the positive framing.

---

## Disagreement 19 — v.28: workshop conditions for the smith

- All three describe heat, noise, and focus; minor word differences.
- Key: "deafens" (EMET) vs. "rings in his ears" (LOGOS) vs. "pounds in his ears" (PNEUMA).
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the noise of the hammer deafens him" — "deafens" is the strongest and most precise.

---

## Disagreement 20 — v.28b: polishing the work

- **EMET:** "give it a finished appearance"
- **LOGOS:** "polish it"
- **PNEUMA:** "produce a fine piece"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "give it a polished finish" — combines both senses.

---

## Disagreement 21 — v.33: "decisions of the covenant" vs. "covenant of judgment" vs. "legal decisions"

- **EMET:** "they do not understand the covenant of judgment"
- **LOGOS:** "they do not understand legal decisions"
- **PNEUMA:** "they can't interpret laws"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "they do not understand the decisions of the covenant" — the phrase refers to the Torah's legal rulings; "covenant" should be retained to preserve the specifically Jewish context.

---

## Disagreement 22 — v.34: "keep stable the fabric of the world" vs. "sustain the fabric"

- **EMET:** "they keep stable the fabric of the world"
- **LOGOS:** "they uphold the fabric of this age"
- **PNEUMA:** "they hold the world together"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "they sustain the fabric of this world" — "sustain" combines EMET's stability and LOGOS's "uphold"; "this world" is more concrete than "this age" (LOGOS's αἰών-influenced reading).
